question: Assume today is 2026-10-19. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate Mexico's total merchandise exports in September 2026, in US dollars (original figures, not seasonally adjusted), as they will be first reported in INEGI's timely trade balance bulletin (Balanza Comercial de Mercancías de México, información oportuna).

target.what: Total value of Mexico's merchandise exports (all commodities, f.o.b.) for the calendar month of September 2026, as first published in INEGI's timely merchandise trade balance bulletin (Balanza Comercial de Mercancías de México, información oportuna), original (not seasonally adjusted) figures, in cu
target.publisher: INEGI (Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía), with SAT/ANAM customs data; timely bulletin 'Balanza Comercial de Mercancías de México, información oportuna'
target.cadence: Monthly, released roughly 3-4 weeks after month end (typically late October for September)
target.caveats: Working interpretation: total merchandise exports, f.o.b., all destinations, original figures as first reported (not seasonally adjusted, not the later revised series). The September 2026 bulletin would normally be published around late October 2026, i.e., after the 2026-10-19 cutoff, so the target

candidates.hypothesis: September exports follow a recurring seasonal pattern relative to August and to the same month of prior years; the most recent published months (July/August 2026) anchor the level, and the September/August ratio from prior years transfers the seasonal step.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total merchandise exports (original, USD) from INEGI timely bulletins for Jan 2023 through the latest month published before 2026-10-19 (likely August 2026), plus September values for 2023, 2024, 2025 to compute September/August ratios and year-over-year growth.
search_hints: INEGI balanza comercial mercancías información oportuna exportaciones septiembre

candidates.perspective: US Census/BEA US imports from Mexico
candidates.hypothesis: The large majority of Mexico's exports go to the US; US goods imports from Mexico for September 2026 (Census FT900 advance or BEA) track Mexico's exports with a stable ratio, allowing a bridge: Mexico exports ≈ US imports from Mexico / US share.
candidates.data_to_find: US Census Bureau advance goods trade balance / FT900 US imports from Mexico for September 2026 (released ~late Oct, may be after cutoff — use August 2026 and prior months), and the historical ratio of Mexico's reported exports to US-reported imports from Mexico.

candidates.hypothesis: Total exports = oil exports (Pemex) + non-oil exports (manufacturing, auto, agriculture); estimating each component from its own recent trend and summing gives the total.
candidates.data_to_find: Recent monthly values and trends for Mexican oil exports (Pemex crude value/volume) and non-oil/manufacturing exports (auto sector, electronics) for mid-2026, plus September seasonal factors per component.

candidates.perspective: Cross-border truck/rail freight and port throughput
candidates.hypothesis: Physical throughput at key border crossings (Laredo, El Paso) and ports (Lázaro Cárdenas, Manzanillo) plus auto rail shipments scales with export value via a value-per-unit factor.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly truck crossings and rail carloads at major US-Mexico border crossings for September 2026, port container/tonnage throughput, and a value-per-crossing or per-ton conversion from historical data.
search_hints: Laredo border crossings truck volume September 2026

candidates.hypothesis: Published forecasts or nowcasts of Mexico's September 2026 trade balance/exports (e.g., Banxico, private analysts, IMF Article IV) constrain the level; treat as forecast, not realization.
candidates.data_to_find: Any forecast or nowcast of Mexico September 2026 exports or trade balance published before 2026-10-19, and Banxico's recent trade balance commentary.

candidates.hypothesis: US tariff actions, USMCA review, or auto-sector disruptions in 2026 shift the level and seasonal ratio of Mexican exports; quantify exposure to adjust the historical seasonal route.
candidates.data_to_find: Any 2026 US tariff measures affecting Mexican goods, auto-sector production/shipment data, and reported month-on-month export changes in mid-2026 to gauge the shock magnitude.

candidates.hypothesis: The September-to-August export ratio and September year-over-year growth have stable historical distributions; use these base rates applied to the latest known monthly level.
candidates.data_to_find: Historical September/August export ratios and September YoY growth rates for Mexico for 2015-2025 (original figures), to establish mean and variability.

kept.rationale: August 2026 total exports grew 40.4% y/y, an exceptional surge; September 2026 light-vehicle exports fell ~12% y/y and manufacturing activity was flat, so September total growth should be well below August's but still positive. A factor of 0.5 (i.e., ~20% y/y growth) with a wide range captures the u
kept.applies_when: September 2026 total export growth is a fraction of August's exceptional growth, consistent with the auto drag.
kept.falsified_by: September 2026 total exports growing at or above August's 40.4% rate, or falling outright.

kept.name: Mexico-reported exports to US-reported imports from Mexico ratio (f.o.b./customs basis)
kept.rationale: Mexico's August 2026 exports (78.0 bn) exceed US-reported imports from Mexico (60.64 bn) by a factor of ~1.29, reflecting f.o.b. vs customs-value and origin-rule differences. This ratio is used to convert US imports into Mexico exports for the d2 bridge.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
